title: Why a Yawn Spreads Like a Cold
topic: Why do you yawn when someone else yawns?

lines: Ever wonder why a single yawn can spark a chain reaction?
Seeing someone yawn triggers a reflex in our brain that mirrors theirs.
The visual cue activates mirror neurons, sending a signal to the yawning centre.
Scientists think the reflex helps cool the brain—cold packs cut contagion dramatically.
In experiments, cold forehead packs reduced contagious yawning to about nine percent.

beats.title: Social Bond Boosts Contagion
lines: The more socially close you are, the faster you catch the yawn.
Studies on wolves and dogs show the same pattern—close bonds boost contagion.
Try breathing through your nose next time and see if the yawn stops!

sources.claim: Seeing someone yawning triggers a reflex in our brain that mirrors theirs and activates mirror neurons.
Cold forehead packs reduced contagious yawning to about nine percent, while warm packs kept it around forty‑one percent.
Social closeness increases contagious yawning in wolves and dogs, linking it to empathy.
